claim: Gittins index policy is optimal for independent arms with discounting when only the played arm changes; it is only a heuristic for restless bandits.
agent_test: Not directly testable; use as framing: allocate by index per option, not by mean.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Cumulative-regret-optimal rules (UCB, Thompson) have logarithmic regret, but they are the wrong target when only the final answer matters: low cumulative regret forces polynomial, not exponential, decay of simple regret.
agent_test: Same-token test: UCB-style allocation vs uniform vs successive halving for choosing a final answer among candidates.
audit_note: Listed a25 url (1603.06560) is Hyperband, not a synthesis; claim does not depend on it.

claim: Fixed-confidence best-arm identification with Track-and-Stop needs about half the draws of KL-LUCB (3968 vs 8437 on a 4-arm instance); re-checked in the paper table.
agent_test: Compare stopping rules on candidate-solution selection at equal tokens.

claim: Successive halving and Hyperband give large speedups (6x to 70x vs random search; about 10x vs Bayesian optimisation) but can lose when early performance does not predict final (SVHN: SMAC beat Hyperband).
agent_test: Run N drafts, cut the worst half after short partial reasoning; check rank correlation of early vs final correctness.

claim: Off-the-shelf LLMs do not explore robustly in bandits from raw history: of 72 GPT-4 prompt configurations only one (BSSC0: summarised stats, hint, CoT, T=0) avoided suffix failure; no GPT-3.5 or Llama2 configuration did.
agent_test: Replicate with current models on a K=5 gap-0.2 bandit with tool-computed per-arm means.

claim: For Gemini-1.5 Flash and Pro, giving externally computed per-arm statistics (summarised history or UCB statistics in the prompt) raises bandit performance (MAB win rate Flash 27.7 to 32.2-34.8, Pro 45.5 to 59.6-60.0); raw history is poor, and in contextual bandits raw history is near useless (Flash 0.0, Pro 7.1 vs 46.4, 64.3 with algorithm-guided support). The small Gemma models did not benefit.
agent_test: Scaffold test: external tally of option outcomes vs raw transcript, equal tokens.
audit_note: Numbers match EVOLvE Table 1 (contextual RH Flash 0.0, Pro 7.1; AG 46.4, 64.3), but external statistics helped only the larger Gemini models: for Gemma-2B and Gemma-9B summarised or algorithm-guided win rates were lower than raw history (SH 10.5/5.3 and AG 4.9/4.1 vs RH 7.6/10.5; AG below RH for Gemma-9B). Metric is pairwise win rate.
claim_before_audit: Giving the LLM externally computed per-arm statistics (summarised history or UCB stats in the prompt) raises exploration; raw history is poor, and in contextual bandits raw history is near useless (Flash 0.0, Pro 7.1 vs 46.4, 64.3).

claim: Fine-tuning on UCB trajectories lifted Gemini Flash to 65.6% MAB win rate; few-shot demos help small models but hurt the large one (Pro). Fine-tuning is not usable for a training-free scaffold, but warns against naive few-shot.
agent_test: Check whether few-shot allocation examples hurt a strong model in our scaffold.

claim: Weak models stay on linear regret in bandits (Gemma-2B, 9B); stronger models (Gemini Pro) with support reach near-sublinear regret.
agent_test: Measure regret slope per model size at fixed horizon.

claim: LLMs are greedy: they under-explore, show frequency bias and a knowing-doing gap (correct rationale 87%, greedy action in 64% of those).
agent_test: Add a forced-exploration rule (try each option once, or bonus for untried) and compare coverage.
audit_note: 87% and 64% figures are from Gemma2 models (largest), not LLMs in general.

claim: An exploration bonus (+1 reward for untried actions) in RL fine-tuning raised arm coverage from 50% to 70%; chain of thought is a key exploration mechanism (no CoT: 25% coverage vs 40-65%). Gap search: a try-all first pass was the single biggest regret gain of seven mechanisms in the same paper (fine-tuning setting, not prompt-only).
agent_test: Prompt-level analogue: require an untried-option check before committing.

claim: GPT-3 has lower regret than humans on the horizon task (2.72 vs 3.24) yet shows no directed exploration and ignores horizon; old model, easy task.
agent_test: Re-run the horizon task with a current model and a reasoning model.

claim: Showing earlier bandit tasks in context improves later ones (meta-in-context learning); GPT-3 matched Greedy after four tasks.
agent_test: Test whether earlier-problem outcomes in context improve later allocation.

claim: LLMs show optimism bias in two-option learning, flipping with counterfactual feedback, qualitatively like humans.
agent_test: Check optimism in the agent's self-estimates of option value.

claim: Pretrained LLMs often reach sublinear regret in full-feedback online learning, but GPT-4 fails simple adversarial sequences (alternating, adaptive); linear regret not rejected over 20 runs. Gap search: with raw history GPT-4 handled the canonical follow-the-leader counterexample and the switch-at-c sequence; it failed only the noisy alternating and adaptive-loss sequences.
agent_test: Adversarial-switch test: option payoffs flip; does the agent notice.

claim: Whether summarised history is the key to exploration is contested: Krishnamurthy (stochastic bandit) says yes; Park et al. found raw vs summary changed regret in online learning (p=1.2e-157) but state the settings differ.
agent_test: Run both input formats on both task types.

claim: Reasoning models explore far better than standard LLMs in open-ended search (Little Alchemy 2, 500 trials: o1 177, R1 85, humans 42, GPT-4o 35, Llama-70B 25, 8B 9); a prompt reminding to vary gave no gain, higher temperature a small one.
agent_test: Compare thinking-on vs off at equal token budget on an open-ended search.

claim: More samples raise coverage log-linearly (SWE-bench Lite 15.9% to 56% at 250 samples; MATH Llama-3-8B 82.9% at 100 to 98.44% at 10,000) but majority vote and reward models do not convert coverage into accuracy (40.50% to 41.41%): value depends on a verifier.
agent_test: Equal-token best-of-N with and without a verifier.
audit: downgraded 2026-11-01 by check_established.py: only 1 opened source(s) from distinct authors

claim: Allocating test-time compute per prompt by difficulty beats uniform best-of-N: Snell about 4x less compute, Damani up to 50% less on code and math, Zuo and Zhu up to +11.1 points on MATH-500; nothing helps at the hardest level.
agent_test: Difficulty-routed token budget vs flat budget at equal total tokens.
audit_note: Zuo and Zhu 11.10% is a coverage gain at average budget 8 on Llama-3.1-8B (accuracy gains are 1.4 to 2.5 points); nothing-helps-at-level-5 is Snell saying no method makes meaningful progress.

claim: Adaptive stopping of repeated sampling saves samples with small loss: Adaptive-Consistency up to 7.9x fewer samples with under 0.1% drop; early-stopping self-consistency cuts 34% to 84%; mid-generation pruning drops 50-75% of samples. Gap search: savings shrink on hard sets (ESC cuts MATH by 33.8% vs GSM8K by 80.1%), and confidence-based cutting can lose accuracy when the model is confidently wrong (DeepConf).
agent_test: Stop self-consistency when the lead is safe; measure accuracy per token.

claim: Many hard problems have zero success probability (about 50% of coding problems in one set), so detecting hopeless arms can free budget; difficulty predictors reach 72-84% accuracy.
agent_test: Early-abandon test with a give-up option; check false-abandon rate.

claim: Bandit-style selection among prompts or search branches works: TRIPLE sequential halving beat uniform by 15% and UCB by 5-6% at budget 150; LATS (UCT tree search) reached 92.7 HumanEval Pass@1 with GPT-4.
agent_test: Use halving over candidate plans at equal tokens against uniform.
audit_note: Gains are average relative improvements over baselines in the paper.

claim: Humans combine UCB-like directed and Thompson-like random exploration (hybrid model, exceedance 0.999); older adults explore less, and about 26% avoid information.
agent_test: Design the agent policy as bonus plus noise, not either alone.
audit_note: Older adults showed similar directed exploration but lower random exploration and less information seeking; the 26% is from the abstract while the results section gives 11 of 51 (21.6%).

claim: Transformers trained on bandit histories imitate Thompson or UCB in context.
agent_test: Out of scope for a training-free scaffold.

claim: Reasoning models raise directed exploration as thinking grows (o3-mini high exceeded humans, Gemini-2.5-flash approached humans), but in a non-stationary 4-armed bandit all LLMs still showed worse directed exploration than humans. No test on the Krishnamurthy hard instance with raw history was found.
agent_test: Run the hard-bandit raw-history test with thinking off, low, high; record SuffFailFreq and thinking tokens.

claim: A scaffold that makes the LLM implement posterior sampling in separate steps (update counts, sample, act) beat prompt-only LLM agents and was not beaten by swapping in R1: explicit allocation steps matter more than raw thinking tokens.
agent_test: Compare a written tally plus sample-and-act step against free thinking at equal tokens.

claim: Reasoning models can exploit from raw history (GPT-5-mini perfect on the simple highest-mean-arm puzzle), while GPT-4 and GPT-3.5 fail it; the weak link in end-to-end bandits is the decision to explore, and LLMs still lose to linear regression on contextual tasks.
agent_test: Give the model the exploit step only; let a rule schedule exploration.

claim: Prompt-level forced exploration has support but no clean prompt-only test: try-all-first gave the biggest gain in the fine-tuned Gemma study, and random subsampling of the context raised exploration and stability in ICRL (Qwen2.5-7B 6.2% to 72.2%). Whether a prompt-only try-each-once rule keeps accuracy on frontier models is untested.
agent_test: A/B on frontier model: add 'try each option once' rule vs none, compare coverage and final accuracy.

claim: Allocators that need the LLM's own success estimate inherit its overconfidence: verbalised confidence sits at 80-100% (older models); reasoning models calibrate better (33 of 36 settings) and improve along the chain; a wrong near-zero estimate sends budget to hopeless options.
agent_test: Cap spend per option and rely on observed counts rather than stated priors.
audit_note: Damani predictor is a hidden-state probe, not the LLM stated estimate; the 1% vs 0% pathology is real but concerns a learned predictor, so the framing is a synthesis.

claim: Early partial reasoning is a usable but imperfect predictor of final correctness: probe accuracy about 65% at 10% of a chunk, 79% peak; consistency-based pruning (ST-BoN) matches full best-of-N at 20-30% of the cost. No rank correlation after k tokens for black-box prompts was found.
agent_test: Probe the model for its current answer every k tokens; cut only when the answer is stable and confidence is high.
audit_note: Zhang gives decrements of 14% from a 79% peak (read as points, giving 65%); ST-BoN 70-80% savings holds at certain N values; the no-rank-correlation sentence is an absence claim.

claim: Early cutting fails when early rank does not predict final rank: Hyperband on SVHN was beaten by SMAC with early stopping, and the most exploratory bracket was nearly best; DeepConf lost accuracy at its aggressive 10% filter because of confident wrong traces.
agent_test: Use conservative cut levels; keep one exploratory bracket (many starts, little cutting).

claim: No published measurement of an LLM using a Gittins or Whittle index was found on arXiv; non-stationary LLM-bandit work uses UCB or Thompson with forgetting (ParetoBandit).
agent_test: Compute an index per option outside the model and test it against UCB under switching cost.

claim: Non-stationary or reactive payoffs break LLM allocators in specific ways: GPT-4 fails noisy alternating and adaptive losses, raw history beats summaries on the switch sequence, and basic LLMs show higher regret than humans in a drifting 4-armed task. Forgetting on per-arm statistics (ParetoBandit) is a known bandit-side fix; no scaffold-only LLM fix has been measured.
agent_test: Switch test: payoffs flip at a hidden time; compare cumulative tally, decayed tally and raw recent history.

claim: Bandit allocation over candidate programs reduces calls 1.5x-5x when a verifier supplies the reward (REx), with no gain on easy problems. Multi-round successive halving over candidates with a weak or absent verifier at equal total tokens has not been measured.
agent_test: Equal-token comparison: halving vs uniform best-of-N vs difficulty routing with a noisy verifier.

claim: Stop rules lose most where they are needed most: self-consistency early stopping saves 80% on GSM8K but 34% on MATH; weak models with near-zero accuracy run to the cap. Savings do not shrink accuracy much on average.
agent_test: Add a give-up rule next to the stop rule for items with low early agreement.

claim: Bookkeeping cost: written tallies work in short horizons (Beta counts in words, T=100) but a prompt with full history grows linearly (5,000-8,000 tokens per call at T=100 in one setting), so tool-computed statistics are needed for long runs. A head-to-head of self-written vs tool tally was not found.
agent_test: Same task with tool-kept stats, self-written tally, and raw history; count tokens and regret.
